design_rationale: WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST: the surface goal ('activate the Elite Specialty Coaching package I applied for') never names sessions_granted, forfeited_sessions or closed_date; the agent must read pt_ext_purchase_pricing's rule to learn that activation is blocked while the member's open-package count (including the application itself) exceeds max_per_customer, discover that OLD_PTH is stale per pt_package_expiration_policy, and resolve that chain (lapse then archive) before activation's own signing-bonus calculation is correct at handling time. This is long (lapse -> archive -> activate is a strict 3-deep chain, each link's resolution changing what the next link may legally do) and broad (pt_ext_lapse_forfeit reads membership CPARAM for its grace credit, pt_ext_archive_closed reads membership CFIELD for its tenure check, pt_ext_purchase_pricing reads membership CPARAM again for its signing bonus; history reconciliation over 8 pre-existing pt_session_redeemed rows on the stale package). SCOPE CLAIMED: this task claims the whole chain rooted at pt_ext_purchase_pricing -- pt_ext_archive_closed and pt_ext_lapse_forfeit as its transitive prerequisites -- disjoint from task 0's workflow and its four policies (pt_ext_late_cancel_fee, pt_ext_refund, pt_ext_bonus_loyalty, pt_ext_trainer_reassignment), which govern pt_session_cancelled_late/pt_package_refunded/pt_bonus_session_granted/pt_trainer_reassigned exclusively; this task governs pt_package_lapsed/pt_package_expired/pt_package_archived/pt_package_activated exclusively. No tool, policy or event type is shared between the two tasks. BASE-INVARIANT CARD: pt_package_expiration_policy's expiration_window_elapsed eligibility (applies_to pt_package_lapsed) anchors on OLD_PTH's own opened_date=2025-02-02 with duration_source=expiration_window_days=180 (20-Session Performance Pack), relation not_before, boundary inclusive: 2025-02-02+180d=2025-08-01; frozen_time date 2025-09-10 is well past that boundary -- satisfied (a case at 2025-08-01 exactly would still pass since the boundary is inclusive; a case at 2025-07-31 would fail). pt_agg_multi_holding's cap (max_per_customer=2) is confirmed violated at the opening: OLD_PTH (active), CUR_PTH (active) and NEW_PTH (applied) are all non-closed, three open holdings against a cap of 2 -- this is the world fact this task's extended eligibility (activation must not leave the count over max_per_customer) reads. pt_specialty_membership_gating's purchase_requires_qualifying_membership is confirmed satisfied (membership active at Black Card All-Access, rank 6 >= minimum_membership_tier_rank 4 for Elite Specialty Coaching), though this gate formally applies to pt_package_purchased, which already happened before this call (NEW_PTH was seeded as applied). WORLD ROW LOAD-BEARING ROLES: the 8 pre-existing pt_session_redeemed rows on OLD_PTH explain why its sessions_remaining reads 12 rather than 20 (8 consumed of 20 included); CUR_PTH exists purely to make the open-package count exceed the cap of 2 at the opening (delete it and the count would only be 2 even before archiving OLD_PTH, and the cap prerequisite would already be satisfied vacuously -- CUR_PTH is therefore load-bearing on the prerequisite's own unresolved-at-opening status, not on any compute value). The active membership (Black Card All-Access, personal_training_discount_pct=15) is load-bearing on two independent computations: it supplies pt_ext_lapse_forfeit's grace credit (int(12*15/100)=1, forfeiting 11 instead of 12) and pt_ext_purchase_pricing's signing bonus (15>=10 threshold, +2 sessions, granting 22 instead of 20); removing the membership row would change both. Membership tenure (200 days, opened 2025-02-22) comfortably clears pt_ext_archive_closed's own min_membership_age_for_backdate_days=30 threshold, making established_membership genuinely true and therefore genuinely load-bearing: forcing the membership factor off would flip backdate_ok false and change closed_date from 2025-08-01 to frozen_time's own date. The not_backdatable branch itself stays untriggered in this world -- the required untriggered branch on that key computation. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: OLD_PTH is the sole target of the lapse and archive writes, correlated throughout by pt_holding_id; NEW_PTH is the sole target of the activation write; CUR_PTH is never touched by any gold write, distinguishable from OLD_PTH by its own pt_holding_id and its unrelated variant/history. PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root_problem=pt_ext_purchase_pricing (the customer's surface request -- activate the applied package). Two prerequisites, chained: (1) pt_ext_archive_closed, kind=state_gate, gate=pt_agg_multi_holding.max_per_customer -- unresolved at frozen_time because OLD_PTH, CUR_PTH and NEW_PTH together are 3 non-closed holdings against a cap of 2; resolved by archive_pt_package_1350ea96, which closes OLD_PTH and brings the count to 2. (2) pt_ext_lapse_forfeit, kind=value_input (a prerequisite of pt_ext_archive_closed, transitively of the root), gate=result -- unresolved at frozen_time because OLD_PTH's status is still 'active' rather than 'expired', so pt_ext_archive_closed's own forfeiture_recorded binding reads false and its result binding would compute frozen_time's date (2025-09-10) rather than OLD_PTH's own expiration_date (2025-08-01); resolved by lapse_expire_package_bc252d9e. Since this is a strict chain (not a fan-out), resolution_order is unique: lapse, then archive, then activate -- there is no second valid ordering to prove equivalent. NO_USER_HINT: user_scenario (below) never names a lapse, an archive, a session cap, or any prerequisite; Marcus only ever states his own situation, and mentions the old Performance Pack only as a forgotten, unrelated fact when asked, never as something he thinks needs fixing. TOOLS_DO_NOT_BLOCK: neither lapse_expire_package_bc252d9e nor archive_pt_package_1350ea96 nor activate_pt_package_46fb321d checks any precondition in task_tools.py -- each simply looks up the holding by id and writes; an agent that called activate_pt_package_46fb321d before resolving either prerequisite would still get a normal confirmation string back, just with a lower, wrong sessions_granted computed at the wrong handling time and OLD_PTH left open, which only the terminal-hash comparison catches. STANDARD SOLUTION: locate and verify Marcus; read his packages, history and membership; recognize from pt_package_expiration_policy that OLD_PTH has lapsed and lapse it; recognize from pt_ext_purchase_pricing's rule that the open-package count (OLD_PTH+CUR_PTH+NEW_PTH=3) exceeds the cap and archive OLD_PTH; then activate NEW_PTH with the handling-time-correct sessions_granted and expiration_date. VERIFICATION (executed by hand against this exact seed, reproduced here): lapse -- current_remaining=12, membership_pt_disc=15, grace_credit=int(12*15/100)=1, forfeited=max(0,12-1)=11. archive -- forfeiture_recorded=true (status now expired), backdate_ok=true, not_backdatable=false, result=OLD_PTH's own expiration_date=2025-08-01. activate -- sessions_included=20 (Elite), is_unlimited=false, membership_active=true, membership_pt_disc=15, threshold=10, qualifies_bonus=(true and 15>=10)=true, does_not_qualify=false, bonus_sessions=2, result=20+2=22; expiration_date=NEW_PTH's own opened_date (2025-09-07) + expiration_window_days=180 = 2026-03-06. Skip-lapse sensitivity on archive: with lapse skipped, current_status stays 'active', forfeiture_recorded=false, long_tenured=false (tenure 200<365), backdate_ok=false, not_backdatable=true, result=frozen_time's date 2025-09-10, not 2025-08-01 -- confirming the value_input edge is load-bearing. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT ONLY: reading only the published rule prose, the tool schemas and Marcus's own lines (masking compute/expected/GT), the same three numbers are re-derivable: the chain is stated in general prose reachable from each policy's own rule field once rendered, the read tools return the same rows, and no second candidate action or object exists in this world -- agreement confirmed.
user_scenario: Marcus Webb calls sounding upbeat and ready to get going. He's been a Black Card member for years and says he wants to activate the Elite Specialty Coaching package he applied for -- he signed up for it a few days ago but it never went through, so he'd like it finished today. He's happy for the representative to look at his account and set everything up; he doesn't need to do anything himself. If asked to verify who he is, he gives his mobile number, 5555550233, and, if asked for a second detail, his date of birth, 1979-11-02 (November 2nd, 1979); he doesn't offer his email or photo id unless specifically asked for those instead. If asked whether he currently holds any other personal-training package, he mentions, a little sheepishly, that he thinks he still has an old Performance Pack on his account from earlier in the year, but he hasn't been in for a session on it in months -- he'd honestly forgotten about it until asked. If asked who he'd like as his trainer for the new package, he says Elena Cho -- that's who he requested when he first signed up. He doesn't ask about his membership or bring up any billing detail beyond wanting the new package activated; he has no opinion on how the old package gets handled and doesn't ask about it further. Once the representative tells him the new package is active, he thanks them and says that's everything -- he doesn't ask for a receipt to be sent anywhere, doesn't bring up any other topic, and ends the call satisfied.
